workload.document_keys: synthetic distinct keys; no document bodies

method: Same harness in both trees. Alternate baseline/candidate order; replay has one untallied warm-up per process. Every persisted vector dataset is reread and validated. Journal setup excluded from replay timing; vector checkpoint reported separately.
limitations: Native macOS ARM64 shared host; no Docker CPU/memory envelope or OpenAI calls.
Replay timings include diagnostic allocator overhead; vector timing runs use the original uninstrumented SMP allocator.
Allocation counts cover the passed allocator, not every direct libc allocation; peak requested live bytes are not RSS.
No measured reduction in peak live heap. Single-record-per-document replay timing is variable; do not claim zero overhead.

Text/algebraic replay timing uses a validating consumer and excludes downstream document parsing/indexing. Graph and full-document throughput have not been benchmarked; real-body correctness is checked separately by database integration fixtures.

budget_regressions: Descriptor admission/deduplication during collection; finish requires no new admission.
Slice and aggregate hard limits with complete replay progress for text/algebraic/dense/sparse document descriptors.
Full item windows stop before decoding oversized lookahead; admission-denied lookahead yields an already collected window.
Deferred and admission-denied records retain their cursor position and replay exactly once after retry.
Oversized full-text records that fit the hard budget apply bounded subchunks before advancing the record sequence.

budget_fix_followup.method: Seven measured samples and one untallied warm-up in each process; journal setup once per variant/case. Variant order alternates between cases, not between samples. Same diagnostic counter and validating consumer; shared macOS host. Timings are diagnostic and exclude indexing.
budget_fix_followup.candidate_changes: Descriptor admission during collection, lookahead admission yielding, decoder credit release, bounded headroom checks.
limitations: Integration compilation and unrelated workloads were active on the shared host; timing changes are diagnostic, not a throughput guarantee.
Seven measured samples per variant/case reuse the journal in one process; these are not seven alternating paired process runs.
Allocation counts and peak requested live bytes are identical to the original candidate measurements for all six remeasured cases.

streaming_key_pool_followup.method: Three alternating baseline/candidate pairs per source/index kind/record size/window size/budget case. Each process performs one untallied warm-up then one measured replay. Setup excluded. Identical source-aware harnesses in both worktrees. All cases validate document counts/checksums, zero live counted allocations, and released reservations.
limitations: Native macOS ARM64 shared host; compilation and unrelated work were active. Instrumented timings are diagnostic and do not establish zero overhead.
Replay measures key construction and binary decoding with a validating synchronous consumer. Body decoding, downstream indexing, embeddings and external API calls excluded.

Primary-store uses the in-memory backend with hinted replay entries; journal uses in-memory LSM/WAL. These are separate sources; journal suffix-copy savings do not apply to the already streaming primary-store cursor.
Only requested allocation bytes through the passed allocator are counted, not all backend allocations or process RSS. Pooled key blocks can increase requested bytes through spare capacity.
Vector preparation unchanged in this follow-up; original real-file vector measurements preserved. Graph throughput, full-body throughput and Linux 0.5 CPU / 2 GB Docker are not benchmarked.

enrichment_compact_followup.method: Identical operation-aware benchmark harnesses in baseline and candidate. Replay validates counts/targets and the fixture-derived expected checksum. Enrichment validates group counts/checksums and each latest sequence. Latest-sequence scans validate the returned sequence. All operations release counted allocations and reservations. Alternating baseline/candidate order, one untallied warm-up and one measured sample per process; setup excluded. Bulk and single-document replay use five pairs per case; enrichment and latest scans use three. Replay was remeasured after the final hot-path changes; those changes do not affect enrichment/latest scans. Enrichment/latest run without a replay ResourceManager.
limitations: Native macOS ARM64, Zig 0.16.0, ReleaseFast. Shared-host compilation and other benchmark processes were active; timings are diagnostic and do not establish zero overhead.
Replay construction and source scans only; document-body decoding, indexing, graph throughput, external embeddings/generation, Linux Docker CPU/RAM limits excluded.

Requested bytes through the passed allocator only, not all backend allocations or process RSS. Zero counted allocations in latest journal scans means payload copies are eliminated, not that backend transactions allocate nothing.
Vector preparation unchanged in this follow-up; original vector measurements preserved.

Single-document replay allocation counts/bytes/peak are unchanged; median elapsed times increased 1.4–4.1%, with paired medians +0.8–3.7%. Primary latest-scan timings approach clock resolution; percentages are not useful there.
